children: State Bank of India, the country’s largest lender, has handed over a cheque worth ₹500 crore to Jeevika Didis in Patna.

The symbolic cheque was handed over to Jeevika Didis by SBI Chairman C S Setty during a Self-Help Group (SHG) mega credit outreach camp, titled “Swavalamban 2026”, organised by the bank’s Patna Circle, on Friday.

In Bihar, “Jeevika Didi” refers to women members of State government initiative Bihar Rural Livelihoods Project (BRLP), locally known as “Jeevika”, aimed at the social and economic empowerment of rural women through Self-Help Groups. The SHG members arrived from various districts of the State to attend the event.

Notably, the Bihar Government, through the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS), an autonomous body under the Department of Rural Development, is spearheading the World Bank aided initiative.

During the event on Friday, C S Setty, the SBI Chairman, Himanshu Sharma, CEO, Jeevika, and Anurag Joshi, Chief General Manager, SBI, Patna Circle, among others, addressed  Jeevika Didis, the bank said in a release.
In his address, Setty appreciated the initiatives undertaken jointly by SBI and Jeevika for women’s empowerment and emphasized the need to further strengthen these efforts in the future.

Sharma outlined the various initiatives being undertaken by Jeevika for the economic empowerment of women and urged the bank to play an active role in the implementation of these programs. Joshi presented a detailed account of the efforts made by the bank for SHGs in Patna Circle and assured that these initiatives would be implemented more effectively in the future

title: SBI hands over cheque worth ₹500 crore to Jeevika Didis in Patna
